review_notes: I read the whole target file. It declares no @[simp] lemmas and no simp sets, so I only looked for missing simp lemmas and rewrites that the proofs prove by hand. I read the divBy API in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Localization/Away.lean`, including its existing @[simp] lemmas and `map_divBy_eq_mul_inv`. I found no unwanted expansions or rewrite cycles in the target. The one finding is a local `hdiv` rewrite that looks like a missing canonical lemma for `IsLocalization.Away.lift` on `divBy`. I did not run Lean. Whether the proposed lemma works as a simp lemma (the unit expression and its normal form) is untested, and I could not search for further uses of this pattern across the whole library.

findings.excerpt: have hdiv (t : A) : IsLocalization.Away.lift s hs (divBy t s : S) = φ t * ↑hs.unit⁻¹ :=
findings.problem: The value of `IsLocalization.Away.lift s hs` on a distinguished fraction `divBy t s` is not available as a named simp lemma. The proof therefore builds a local `hdiv` by hand-instantiating the general `map_divBy_eq_mul_inv` with a `lift_comp` hypothesis. It then rewrites with `simpa only [hdiv]`. `map_divBy_eq_mul_inv` takes a hypothesis `hψ` and so cannot be a simp lemma. Plain `simp` on `lift s hs (divBy t s)` has no rule, so every consumer of the canonical lift has to repeat this boilerplate. The `lift` case is the common one, and the same `lift` appears in other files of this library.
findings.proposed_change: In `TauCeti/RingTheory/Localization/Away.lean`, next to `map_divBy_eq_mul_inv`, add a `@[simp]` lemma such as `Away.lift_divBy`. It would state `IsLocalization.Away.lift s hs (divBy t s : S) = g t * ↑hs.unit⁻¹` for `g : A →+* B` and `hs : IsUnit (g s)`. Prove it from `map_divBy_eq_mul_inv` and `IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq`. Then replace `hdiv` and `simpa only [hdiv]` here with `simpa using hpow`, or with `simp only [IsLocalization.Away.lift_divBy]`. The right-hand side is a normal form, since `divBy` and `lift` are eliminated and no rewrite cycle arises. It should be checked that the `.unit` argument unifies up to proof irrelevance.
findings.benefit: Anyone computing the canonical extension on a fraction gets the closed form from `simp`. The universal-property proof no longer needs a local rewriting lemma, and other uses of `Away.lift` on `divBy` can share the same rule.

evidence.excerpt: ψ (divBy t s : S) = φ t * ↑(isUnit_of_comp_algebraMap s hψ).unit⁻¹
